Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

Local-runs: probe — on a detached worktree of the head and a second one at the merge-base (744211fc, which is `origin/main` as the branch was cut; `origin/main` had moved to a2f77f75 when fetched and none of the five files changed on it since), Node v22.23.4, no `node_modules`: `node scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` (exit 0 on both trees; Both worktrees were removed after the runs and the main checkout was not touched.
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md (〈复核归属与资格〉 L21–L27 and the landing-head line L53), .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/project-forms.md (〈信箱 PR〉 L40 and L43), .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/triage-duties.md (L3, L10–L11; six base lines L10–L14 cut), scripts/pm/check-owed-reviews.mjs (`takerOf`, the `handed` reading, the TAKE row's `take:` tail, the triggers battery) and scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs (`HANDOFF_TARGET`, `readContractReviewHandoff`/`contractReviewHandoff`, `MAILBOX_KEYS` two rows, the hand-off battery, doc comments) + read, not reviewed: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/skills.md L20 (the ratchet-payment rule), lanes/triage.md L15, landing-operations.md L84, SKILL.md L35, review-checklist.md, scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs (`MAX_LINE_BYTES`, `EXEMPTION_CLASSES`, `classifyLine`, `wrapLine` and the three ledger rows), package.json L84 (`check:pm-record-recognisers`), card #29667 body, comments 6592453746 (claim) and 6592498626 (widened claim with the seat's three rulings), PR #29686 body and its one comment 6593035754 (the seat's review claim on this head), PR #29190 comment 6574245149 (a live in-flight hand-off line naming `triage`)

Reviewer: an isolated contract reviewer at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER, read-only on GitHub (REST reads only; nothing written, pushed, commented or labelled), fed the card body and comments, the PR body, the net diff against the merge-base, the head's check-runs, contract-review.md (base and head) and review-checklist.md. The PR body's measurements were read as input, not as conclusions; every count below is this review's own measurement. No environment variable value and no model identifier is printed anywhere in this record.

### ① Derived judgments

1. File surface. Two commits (13640c87 rules text, cf3a1395 recognisers and owed-review list; author Claude, no trailer pair, no card relation and no model identifier in either message, `check-commit-card-trailers` exit 0), PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, head repo = base repo, draft, base `main`. `git diff --numstat 744211fc cf3a1395`, the REST file listing and the PR body agree on exactly five paths, +117/−87: contract-review.md +8/−8, project-forms.md +2/−2, triage-duties.md +3/−6, check-owed-reviews.mjs +46/−23, record-recognisers.mjs +58/−48. The claim (6592453746) named five files with `lanes/triage.md`; the widened claim (6592498626) swapped that for `triage-duties.md` L3 and L10–L14 after measuring on `main` that the owed-reviews step lives there (confirmed: `lanes/triage.md` L15 already says PASS/FAIL is the lane's and is untouched). On surface, no path outside it.
2. Every sentence of the rules text against the code, line by line. L21 (the seat reviews in-seat; 429 ⇒ keep the marker, post the hand-off, name a review seat, else a sibling seat): `HANDOFF_TARGET` is `^(review#[1-9][0-9]*|domain:[a-z][a-z0-9._-]*#[1-9][0-9]*)(?![0-9])…`, probed: `review#1`, `domain:ui#2`, `Domain:UI#2` (lower-cased to `domain:ui#2`), `domain:skills#12` read `handed` with `to`; `triage`, `director#1`, `review`, `domain:ui`, `review#0` read `unreadable`. L22 (the template) spells that grammar as `<review#N|domain:<lane>#N>`; true. L23 (an owed head with no record, no live claim and one of (a)(b)(c) ⇒ the lane or a review seat, never triage): `takerOf` returns the hand-off's `to`, else `the domain:<lane> seat or a review seat`, else with the lane seat `stood-down`/`absent` `a review seat, or the domain:<lane> seat next on duty`; the report case asserts no printed `take:` names triage, and the live run printed none. True. L24 (a) and (b), L25 (c): the triggers are unchanged in code except `handoff.state === 'handed'` replacing `'triage'`; the taker strings match the three sentences. True. L26 (read the PR before starting; a record or a live claim ⇒ do not start): `contractReviewClaims` and `locateReviewOfRecord` unchanged. True. **L27 — "同 head 双认 ⇒ 车道胜" — is NOT what the code does.** `contractReviewClaims` still reads `side = readSignatureLine(body)?.lane === 'triage' ? 'triage' : 'lane'` and `holder = live.find(side === 'lane') ?? live[0]`. Probed on the head (and identically at the merge-base): a `domain:ui#2` (sibling) claim posted first and the PR's own `domain:server#1` lane claim posted second ⇒ holder = the sibling, `tie` false; a `review#1` claim first, lane second ⇒ holder = the review seat, `tie` false; only a `triage#1` claim first ⇒ holder = the lane, `tie` true. So for every tie that can still arise under the new rule (lane vs review seat, lane vs sibling seat) the code gives the EARLIEST claim and declares no tie; the lane wins only against triage, which this PR says never claims. The dev's acceptance note states the same; the seat's ruling 2 kept the code untouched. This is a text/code disagreement inside the review surface, judged a must-fix in ④ (M1), and it also makes three adjacent code sentences false: check-owed-reviews.mjs L44–45 "`live` (who holds the head, the lane winning a tie)", both self-test summary strings "the lane winning a tie", and record-recognisers.mjs L949–952 (edited in this diff) "When a lane claim and another claim are both live on one head the LANE wins". L31 (overdue holds listed in the triage round record): `renderRow` still prints `list it in the triage round record` and triage-duties L10 still has triage write a round record; consistent. L53 (landing-head re-review by the lane seat or a review seat under (a)(b)(c)): a rule sentence, no code reads it; consistent with `takerOf`.
3. project-forms.md against `MAILBOX_KEYS`. L40 now carries lane → review seat or sibling seat `Request: contract-review` and the reverse `Notify: contract-review`; `MAILBOX_KEYS` reads `request:contract-review` from `lane` to `a review seat (review#N), or a sibling seat of the lane while none is seated` and `notify:contract-review` from `the review seat or sibling lane seat that rendered the record` to `lane` (probed on both trees; the merge-base had `triage` on both). L43 carries `Request: triage` and `Notify: release-blocker`, whose rows are unchanged. The mailbox battery's both-ways pin (every key named in 〈信箱 PR〉, no other key named there) still passes with the two sentences re-cut. "Unsubscribed only" was dropped from L40 and L47 still carries that rule for every doorbell. Correct, and the seat's ruling 1 (triage sends no review notice) is implemented.
4. triage-duties.md cuts have a home or a reason. Base L10 (run `check-owed-reviews` first, take per contract-review.md, 429 ⇒ keep the marker) is the duty the maintainer removed; the marker and no-downgrade rule live at contract-review.md L21. Base L11 (compare `Head-sha` with the current head; regeneration/prose-only exception) lives at contract-review.md L48–L49. Base L12 (a stale FAIL ⇒ same-round re-review) and L13 (a stale PASS ⇒ note on the PR, delta owed, to this seat or a new hand-off) are triage's own self-review housekeeping; what survives them — a stale triage record's delta re-review goes to the lane or a review seat — is head L11, and the stale reading itself is printed by `check-owed-reviews` (`record stale PASS by …` on four live rows). Base L14 (the per-PR self-review row) is replaced by head L10 (per-lane owed count, report only). Head L3 says 定级复审 so the "复审" that stays with triage (grading review of self-triage findings, L28 and L30) is not read as contract review. No rule is lost; measured by reading each removed line against contract-review.md.
5. Ratchet paid line by line, no re-wrap. `diff` of each whole file against the merge-base shows exactly the lines in the diff and nothing else (16, 4 and 9 differing lines for 8+8, 2+2 and 6+3); every unchanged line is byte-identical. Each edited line is a content edit at its own position, not a re-flow of a neighbour: contract-review.md eight for eight (L21–L27, L53), project-forms.md two for two, triage-duties.md six removed for three added. Added lines measure 118, 142, 118, 118, 119, 120, 120, 118 (contract-review.md), 116, 120 (project-forms.md), 118, 118, 103 (triage-duties.md) bytes. Ceilings 60, 55, 99 are untouched in the ledger; counts 60, 55, 96 (headroom 0, 0, 3). Correct under lanes/skills.md L20.
6. The 142-byte line is a structural exemption, not a widening of a pin. `classifyLine` on head L22 returns `unbreakable` (one code span of 140 bytes; `wrapLine` returns one piece), and `scanLineLengths` lists no offender in any of the three files; the merge-base's L22 (122 bytes, code span 120) was already `unbreakable`. The ratchet has no per-line byte pin, only the 120-byte rule with `EXEMPTION_CLASSES` ("the gate never demands a wrap it cannot produce"), and no ledger row moved. The alternative spellings cost a ceiling line (contract-review.md is at 60/60) or lose the grammar `HANDOFF_TARGET` reads; the template is the one line that must spell it. Legitimate. What it is not: pinned against a constant, unlike the claim and hold templates (self-test lines 2684, 2731 read `contract-review.md` for them verbatim) — see S1.
7. Nothing else on the head names triage as a reviewer, hand-off target or review-notice sender. `git grep` over `.claude`, `AGENTS.md`, `scripts/pm`, `.github`, `docs`, `skills` for 分诊 near 复审/复核/审, `欠审`, `交接行`, `Contract-review-handoff`, `check-owed-reviews` and English `triage` near review/hand-off: every remaining hit says the opposite or is another duty — contract-review.md L23 `⛔ 非分诊`, landing-operations.md L84 `⛔ 非分诊`, SKILL.md L35 `复核非分诊`, lanes/triage.md L15 `契约复核(PASS/FAIL 归车道)`, triage-duties.md L28/L30 (grading review of self-triage findings), SKILL.md L171 and seat-lifecycle.md L89 (the triage audit comment), check-half-states.mjs L15194 (routing an unlabelled card). `check-owed-reviews.mjs` is referenced only by package.json L84 (its self-test), contract-review.md L25/L31 and triage-duties.md L10; `contractReviewHandoff` and `contractReviewClaims` are imported only by `check-owed-reviews.mjs`. Clean.
8. An in-flight `triage` hand-off line hurts no gate. Readers of `contractReviewHandoff`: `check-owed-reviews.mjs` (report-only, exit 0 on every read) and the two self-tests; the hand-off battery still asserts `⛔ no gate reads it` through `locateReviewOfRecord`, and `check-governed-queue-guard` does not import it. On such a line the head reads `unreadable` (the thread names the comment), (a)-by-hand-off does not fire, (a)-by-label and (b)/(c) still do, and the taker is the lane seat or a review seat. The live board has exactly one: PR #29190 comment 6574245149, printed as `hand-off unreadable (6574245149)` on a DONE row whose record is current — no effect. `Request: contract-review` doorbells already addressed `To: triage` are unaffected: `readMailboxLine` does not check `To:` against the table. Harmless; the one visible cost is that a 429 hand-off still open at landing must be re-posted naming a seat, which the dev's acceptance note implies and which the report prints.
9. Self-test pins moved only by added cases. Diff over `scripts/pm`: 22 `t(` lines added, 18 removed, net +4 = 353 − 351 (record-recognisers) + 67 − 65 (check-owed-reviews). Hand-off battery pin 13 → 15 with two new cases (a `Domain:UI#2` target reads and hands; a `triage` line is unreadable, never handed); the closed-set case widened from one shape to `triage`, `director`, `review`, `domain:ui`. Triggers battery pin 8 → 10 with two new cases (a sibling-seat hand-off is the taker; a `triage` hand-off gives no (a) and never a triage taker); every TAKE case now asserts its taker; the report case asserts no `take:` names triage. No pin lowered, no battery removed; the 18 removed `t(` lines are each replaced in place by a renamed or strengthened assertion (verified line by line: the `'triage'` → `'handed'` state, `to`/`taker` added, `MSG(…, 'triage')` → default addressee on two mailbox cases). Both self-tests pass on the head; `pnpm check:pm-record-recognisers`'s four scripts all exit 0 here.
10. The live board. `check-owed-reviews` on the head at record time: two TAKE rows (`#26517 … take: the lane seat or a review seat` — lane unknown, no `domain:*` on its card; `#29628 … take: the domain:server seat or a review seat`), three WAIT, two HELD (this PR among them, `claim live … (lane, 6593035754)`), eight DONE; no row names triage as taker; `triage` appears only as the `Reviewed-by:` of a current record on DONE rows. Reproduces the PR body's acceptance (the board has moved since its reading of 43/18/3).
11. Gates. `check-governed-merges --branch HEAD`: 3 of 5 paths hit the `.claude/**` register, GOVERNED Tier S, 204 changed lines; this record is the one it asks for. Ratchet, id-lint, governed-prose, frame-sync, top-level-keys, symbol-anchors, dispatch-gates, trailers, the four recognisers scripts: all exit 0 locally on the head; the nine commands needing `yaml`/`typescript`/`@changesets/cli` are read from CI, where `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests` and `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` are all `success` on the head.
12. PR body against the head. `Fixes #29667` on the first content line, the right verb: the card's four change items are all on the head (item 4 relocated to `triage-duties.md` by the seat) and the card asks for one PR; no closing keyword near any other number (a case-insensitive scan finds only `Fixes #29667`; `#29242` appears twice as prose). `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are present as their own lines and right (no published package, no spec, no narrowing). The body's numbers (60/60, 55/55, 99→96, 142 vs 122, 353/351, 13→15, 67/65 in 9, 8→10, 40 commands) all reproduce. Its four acceptance notes are accurate; the first is M1. No model identifier in body, title or commits. Labels `documentation`, `size/m`, `skip-changeset`; `mergeable_state` blocked (draft), `auto_merge` null.
13. Nothing new on any surface: no gate, label, patrol row, workflow or package; `TRIAGE_ROUND_MINUTES` keeps its name; `check-owed-reviews` keeps exit 0 on every read. The card's ⛔ holds.

### ② Semver level

None. No published package, no `packages/spec/src/**`, no TypeScript; governed rules text under `.claude/**` plus two `scripts/pm` report-only tools and their self-tests. `skip-changeset` is the right declaration and Check Changeset is `success` on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev acceptance note 1 (`contractReviewClaims` reads only `triage#N` as the non-lane side, so a lane-vs-review tie goes to the earliest claim): confirmed by probe on both trees and raised to M1 — the rule text L27 and three code sentences say the lane wins, the code gives the earliest claim for every tie that can still occur. The seat's ruling 2 kept the code untouched; the reviewer's reading is that the text and the code must agree on the head that lands, and the code is the side to move (④).
- Dev acceptance note 2 (`review#N` is not a `seatKey` spelling, so no doorbell can be addressed `To: review#1` until #29242): accurate; the rule text's fallback (sibling lane seat) is the one that works today, and `HANDOFF_TARGET` reads both shapes already. No flag; #29242 inherits it.
- Dev acceptance note 3 (two WIP commits without the trailer pair; branch is `claude/project-thread-*`, so no force-push to reword): `check-commit-card-trailers` exit 0 — the gate requires no card relation and no model identifier, both satisfied; the dev session is named only in the PR body footer (`session_01J8VVAka2VdDFVA5VvZmmgK`, not the reviewer's). Recorded, not flagged.
- The hand-off template at contract-review.md L22 is not pinned against a constant the way `CONTRACT_REVIEW_CLAIM_TEMPLATE` and `CONTRACT_REVIEW_HOLD_TEMPLATE` are; the grammar lives twice (L22 and `HANDOFF_TARGET`) with nothing holding them together. S1.
- triage-duties.md L10 says the round record counts owed heads older than one round per lane off `check-owed-reviews.mjs`; the script prints the lane on every row and a total `to take`, but no per-lane count — the seat counts rows. The sentence is true of what the seat does with the output, not of a printout. S2 names the one-line report addition that would make the instrument say it.
- triage-duties.md shrank 99 → 96 and its ceiling stayed 99. Lowering is optional in the ratchet ("may be LOWERED"); the PR body says no ceiling row moved. Not flagged.
- Independence: PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, commit author Claude, dev session `session_01J8VVAka2VdDFVA5VvZmmgK` (PR body footer), not the reviewer's; no off-relay author note is owed. The PR thread carries the seat's `Contract-review-claim:` for this head (6593035754) and no other record.
- Governed, Tier S: lands by the owning seat through the queue once a PASS record is on the current head and every check is green. This record is FAIL; the delta commit carrying M1 owes a delta review by the same reviewer.

### ④ Design judgment

Per hits file, against the card's scenario (the maintainer removed triage from contract review; who reviews must be stated once and read the same by the rule text, the hand-off line and the owed-review list) and the card's constraint (no new gate, label or patrol row):

- `references/contract-review.md` 〈复核归属与资格〉: the (a)(b)(c) triggers are kept as triggers and re-pointed from "triage takes" to "the lane or a review seat takes"; keeping them is right because the owed-review list is built on them and the hand-over brief in (c) is where an off-duty lane's heads were always supposed to land. The hand-off template names a seat with a number, so `Reviewed-by:` on the resulting record and the `To:` of the doorbell point at the same thing. Holds, except L27: "同 head 双认 ⇒ 车道胜" is a sentence about what `contractReviewClaims` prints, and on the head it prints the earliest claim for a lane-vs-review or lane-vs-sibling pair. Within the card's rule the side to change is the code, not the text: the text is the ruled rule (6592498626 point 2) and #29242's "earlier claim wins between review seats" is consistent with it (that rule is about two review seats, not a lane and a review seat); the code is a report-only reader whose output no gate consumes, so making it read the PR's lane adds no gate. **M1.**
- `scripts/pm/check-owed-reviews.mjs`: `takerOf` is pure, three strings, and the hand-off's `to` wins over the derived taker, which is the rule's order (a) before the default. Printing `take:` on the TAKE row is the one line a seat reads, and the self-test pins that no printed taker is triage. `TRIAGE_ROUND_MINUTES` keeping its name under a changed doc is right (importers). Holds. The header's "the lane winning a tie" (L44–45) and the summary string restate L27's false sentence; they fall under M1.
- `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs`: `HANDOFF_TARGET` as a closed set of two shapes with the number required is the right grammar — `review` or `domain:ui` without a number would name a lane, not a seat, and `(?![0-9])` keeps `review#1` from matching the head of `review#12`. Reading `triage` as unreadable rather than as a third state is right: a line that hands to nobody must not read as handed, and the self-test proves the thread then names the comment. The `MAILBOX_KEYS` rows move the sender of `notify:contract-review` to the seat that rendered the record, which is the only seat that has the record id the template asks for. Holds. The `contractReviewClaims` doc edited at L949–952 ("another claim … the LANE wins") describes a rule the function below it does not implement; its own doc at L1026–1034 still says the side is triage-or-lane. M1 settles both.
- `references/project-forms.md`: two doorbell legs on L40 and two triage legs on L43 keep the key table at 55/55 with both-ways pinning intact. Dropping "unsubscribed only" from L40 is a correct de-duplication against L47. Holds.
- `references/triage-duties.md`: the two replacement lines are the right residue — triage still produces a round record (L31 of contract-review.md depends on it for overdue holds), so the owed count stays there as a report, and the stale-record case that remains (triage's own old records) is routed by one sentence. Cutting the self-review rows rather than re-pointing them is right, since a seat that reviews nothing has no self-review. Holds (S2 is about what the instrument prints, not the sentence's place).

Must-fix: M1 — make the rule text and the claim reader agree on who holds a tied head, on the code side and with no new gate: in `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs` `contractReviewClaims(rows, headSha, { now, lane })`, read each claim's side off its signature seat as `lane` when the seat is `domain:<lane>#N` for the lane the caller passes (unsigned stays `lane`, as today), `other` for every other signed seat (`review#N`, a sibling `domain:*#N`, `triage#N`); `tie` = a live `lane` and a live `other`; `holder` = the lane's earliest live claim, else the earliest; with no `lane` passed, the earliest. In `scripts/pm/check-owed-reviews.mjs` pass `{ now, lane: lane.lane }` (it already derives the lane via `laneSeatOf`) and correct the header L44–45 and the summary string to "the PR's lane winning a tie"; correct the two doc comments (record-recognisers L949–952 and L1026–1034); add self-test cases in the claim battery: a `review#1` claim first and the lane's claim later ⇒ the lane holds, tie true; a sibling `domain:ui#2` first ⇒ the lane holds; two review seats ⇒ the earliest, no tie; unknown lane ⇒ the earliest, no tie. If the seat instead keeps the code untouched, contract-review.md L27 must say what the code does ("同 head 双认 ⇒ 先贴者持有") — but that contradicts ruling 2, so the code is the side. Should-fix: S1 — pin the hand-off template the way the claim and hold templates are pinned: export `CONTRACT_REVIEW_HANDOFF_TEMPLATE` spelled exactly as contract-review.md L22 inside its code span, add the two self-test cases `the line is spelled VERBATIM … in the rule text` (reading `contract-review.md`) and `the template, sent verbatim, is unreadable` (`readContractReviewHandoff(template).state === 'unreadable'`), so L22 and `HANDOFF_TARGET` cannot drift apart (one existing self-test grows; no new gate). S2 — have `check-owed-reviews` print what triage-duties.md L10 asks the round record to carry: one header line `owed over a round, per lane: domain:server 1 · unknown 1` counting rows with `waited >= TRIAGE_ROUND_MINUTES` and no current record, grouped by `row.lane` (report-only, one case in the report battery).
